extracted.intended_audience: individuals and entities interacting with USPTO under FOIA and the Privacy Act (requesters, submitters, FOIA Officers, Privacy Officer, USPTO staff)
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO FOIA and Privacy Act compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules, definitions, and substantive criteria for handling Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests and Privacy Act inquiries at the United States Patent and Trademark Office, including notice, fee, appeal, and business-information protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of denial letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Denial letters must include an estimate of the volume of records or information withheld (in pages or other reasonable form), unless volume is indicated by deletions in disclosed records or providing an estimate would harm an interest protected by an applicable FOIA exemption; and a statement that the denial may be appealed, plus a list of the requirements for filing an appeal under § 102.10(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The estimate need not be provided in certain circumstances (deletions show volume or estimate would harm exempted interest). The appeal statement must list filing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business information (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Business information means commercial or financial information, obtained by USPTO from a submitter, which may be protected from disclosure under FOIA exemption 4 (5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitter (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitter means any person or entity outside the Federal Government from whom USPTO obtains business information, directly or indirectly; includes corporations; state, local and tribal governments; and foreign governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of business information
rubrics_metrics.description: A submitter should designate by appropriate markings any portions of its submission that it considers protected from disclosure under FOIA exemption 4, at submission or a reasonable time thereafter; such designations expire ten years after submission unless the submitter requests and justifies a longer period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designations should be made promptly and clearly; to extend beyond ten years, submitter must request and provide justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to submitters of FOIA requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The FOIA Officer shall provide a submitter with prompt written notice of a FOIA request or administrative appeal that seeks its business information whenever required under paragraph (e), except as provided in paragraph (h), to give the submitter an opportunity to object to disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be sent via certified mail, return receipt requested, or similar means; when many submitters must be notified, posting or publication reasonably likely to accomplish notification is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When notice is required
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice must be given to the submitter whenever (1) the information has been designated in good faith by the submitter as protected under Exemption 4; or (2) the FOIA Officer has reason to believe the information may be protected under Exemption 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for submitter to object
rubrics_metrics.description: The FOIA Officer must allow a submitter seven working days from receipt of written notice to provide a detailed statement of any objection to disclosure; the statement must specify all grounds for withholding under any FOIA exemption and, for exemption 4, show why the information is a trade secret or commercial/financial information that is privileged or confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond within the time specified will be considered no objection. Information provided by the submitter in this statement may itself be subject to disclosure under FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of intent to disclose business information
rubrics_metrics.description: If the FOIA Officer decides to disclose business information over the submitter's objection, the FOIA Officer shall give the submitter written notice (via certified mail or similar) including: (1) reasons why objections were not sustained; (2) a description of the business information to be disclosed; and (3) a statement that the FOIA Officer intends to disclose the information seven working days from the date the submitter receives the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to submitter-notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice requirements do not apply if: (1) the FOIA Officer determines the information should not be disclosed; (2) the information has been lawfully published or officially made available to the public; (3) disclosure is required by statute (other than FOIA) or regulation under Executive Order 12600; or (4) the submitter's designation appears obviously frivolous (in which case the FOIA Officer shall provide written notice of any final decision to disclose seven working days from receipt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of FOIA lawsuit to submitters
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a requester files a lawsuit seeking to compel disclosure of business information, the FOIA Officer shall promptly notify the submitter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding notice to requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the FOIA Officer provides a submitter notice and opportunity to object under paragraph (d), the FOIA Officer shall also notify the requester(s). Whenever a submitter files a lawsuit seeking to prevent disclosure, the FOIA Officer shall notify the requester(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request is initially denied in whole or in part, or not timely determined, or the requester receives an adverse initial determination regarding matters under §102.7(b), the requester may file a written appeal which must be received by the Office of General Counsel within thirty calendar days of the date of the written denial; if there has been no determination, an appeal may be submitted anytime after the due date, including the last extension under §102.6(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal content and routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals shall be decided by a Deputy General Counsel and should be addressed to the General Counsel, USPTO. The appeal must include a copy of the original request and initial denial, if any, and may include a statement of reasons why records should be made available and why the initial denial was in error. No opportunity for personal appearance, oral argument, or hearing on appeal is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals should be clearly marked 'Freedom of Information Appeal' on both letter and envelope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of granted appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appeal is granted, the appellant shall be immediately notified and copies of releasable documents shall be made available promptly upon receipt of appropriate fees determined under §102.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed exhaustion and right to judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: If no determination on an appeal has been sent within the twenty-working-day period specified in §102.6(b) or the last extension thereof, the requester is deemed to have exhausted administrative remedies, giving rise to a right of judicial review under 5 U.S.C. 552(a)(6)(C). If the requester initiates a civil action based on this provision, the administrative appeal process may continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of adverse appeal determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: A written denial on appeal must include: (1) a brief explanation of the basis for the denial, including a list of applicable FOIA exemptions and a description of how the exemptions apply; (2) a statement that the decision is final; (3) notification that judicial review is available in specified U.S. district courts; and (4) the name and title or position of the official responsible for denying the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging fees in general
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO shall charge for processing FOIA requests in accordance with §102.11(c), except when fees are limited under paragraph (d) or when a waiver/reduction is granted under paragraph (k). USPTO shall collect all applicable fees before sending copies of requested records. Requesters must pay by check or money order payable to the Treasury of the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial use request (definition and handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial use request means a request from or on behalf of a person who seeks information for a use that furthers commercial, trade, or profit interests (including litigation). The FOIA Officer shall determine, when reasonably possible, the use to which a requester will put requested records and provide the requester an opportunity to clarify if it appears the records will be used for commercial purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct costs (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct costs are expenses USPTO incurs in searching for and duplicating (and, for commercial use requests, reviewing) records to respond to a FOIA request; include labor costs (basic rate of pay plus 16% for benefits). Overhead (space, heating, lighting) is not included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplication (definition and format preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplication means making a copy of a record or its information necessary to respond, in forms including paper, microform, audiovisual, or electronic records. The FOIA Officer shall honor a requester's specified preference of form or format if the record is readily reproducible with reasonable efforts in that form or format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of requesters and chargeable fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Four categories: (i) Commercial use requesters — charged search, review, and duplication; (ii) Educational and noncommercial scientific institution requesters — charged duplication (excluding cost of first 100 pages); (iii) Representatives of the news media — charged duplication (excluding cost of first 100 pages); (iv) All other requesters — charged search and duplication (excluding cost of first 2 hours of search and first 100 pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific fee limitations and exemptions described in paragraph (d) modify these charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform fee schedule rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Manual search: actual salary rate of employee involved plus 16% benefits. Computerized search: actual direct cost including operator time. Paper duplication $.15 per page. Other reproduction: actual direct cost. Review: actual salary rate of employee conducting review plus 16% benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fee policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Search fees shall be charged for all requests—other than those by educational institutions, noncommercial scientific institutions, or news media—subject to paragraph (d) limitations. FOIA Officer will charge for time spent searching even if no responsive records are located or located records are entirely exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computerized search costs
rubrics_metrics.description: For computer searches, requesters will be charged the direct costs of conducting the search (including CPU operation and operator/programmer salary), though certain requesters are charged no search fee and others are entitled to the cost equivalent of two hours manual search time without charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplication fee policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplication fees will be charged to all requesters, subject to paragraph (d) limitations. Paper photocopy fee is $.15 per page; copies produced by computer (tapes, printouts) charged direct costs including operator time; other forms charged direct costs of duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one copy need be supplied unless otherwise necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review fee policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Review fees (charged only to commercial use requesters) are charged for the initial record review to determine exemptions and to prepare records for disclosure; review fees are direct costs based on involved employees' labor plus 16%. No charge for review at administrative appeal level for an exemption already applied; subsequent additional review (if an exemption found not applicable) is chargeable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on charging fees
rubrics_metrics.description: No search fee for educational, noncommercial scientific, or news media requesters; no search or review fee charged for a quarter-hour period unless more than half that period is required; except for commercial use requesters, FOIA Officer will provide without charge the first 100 pages of duplication (or equivalent) and the first two hours of search (or equivalent); whenever total fee is $20.00 or less, no fee charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-commercial requesters, no fee will be charged unless search in excess of two hours plus duplication in excess of 100 pages totals more than $20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of anticipated fees over $20
rubrics_metrics.description: When FOIA Officer determines or estimates fees will be more than $20, FOIA Officer shall notify the requester of the actual or estimated fees (unless requester already indicated willingness to pay). The request will not be considered received or processed further until the requester agrees to pay anticipated fees (agreement should be in writing). The notice shall offer opportunity to discuss reformulating the request to reduce cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charges for special services
rubrics_metrics.description: FOIA Officer shall ordinarily charge the direct cost of special services (e.g., certifying that records are true copies or sending records by other than ordinary mail).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest and debt collection
rubrics_metrics.description: FOIA Officer shall charge interest on unpaid bills starting on the 31st calendar day after billing at the rate provided in 31 U.S.C. 3717; shall follow Debt Collection Improvement Act procedures, including use of consumer reporting agencies, collection agencies, and offset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregating requests to prevent fee avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If FOIA Officer reasonably believes a requester or group is dividing a request into a series to avoid fees, FOIA Officer may aggregate requests and charge accordingly. Presumption that multiple related requests within 30 calendar days are to avoid fees; if separated by longer period, aggregate only with solid basis; unrelated matters shall not be aggregated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance payment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: FOIA Officer shall not require advance payment except: (i) if total anticipated fee > $250, requester must pay entire anticipated fee before processing unless satisfactory assurance of payment exists; (ii) if requester previously failed to pay a properly charged FOIA fee within 30 days, FOIA Officer shall require payment of amount due plus interest and an advance payment of anticipated fee before processing a new request; when payment is required, the request is not considered received until payment is received; records are made available only upon receipt of full payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other statutes with separate fee schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: This FOIA fee schedule does not apply to fees charged under any statute (except FOIA) that specifically requires USPTO or another agency to set and collect fees for particular records; FOIA Officer shall inform requesters how to obtain such records from those sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee waiver or reduction criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Records will be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge if FOIA Officer determines that: (1) disclosure is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of Government operations/activities; and (2) disclosure is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requester must demonstrate both prongs; FOIA Officer considers listed factors to determine whether prongs are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to determine public-interest fee waiver — subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor: The subject of the request — whether requested records concern operations or activities of Government with a direct and clear connection, not remote or attenuated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to determine public-interest fee waiver — informative value
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor: The informative value of the information — whether disclosure is 'likely to contribute' to understanding Government operations/activities; disclosable portions must be meaningfully informative and not merely duplicative of publicly available information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to determine public-interest fee waiver — audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor: The contribution to understanding by the public likely to result — whether disclosure will contribute to the understanding of a reasonably broad audience (not just the requester's individual understanding); requester’s expertise and ability/intention to convey information will be considered; news media requesters are presumed to satisfy this consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing information to media alone does not presumptively satisfy this consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to determine public-interest fee waiver — significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor: The significance of the contribution to public understanding — whether disclosure is likely to contribute 'significantly' (i.e., must significantly enhance public understanding compared to prior knowledge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to determine commercial-interest prong of waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor: Existence and magnitude of commercial interest — whether requester has a commercial interest that would be furthered by disclosure; FOIA Officer considers commercial interest of requester and any person on whose behalf requester acts; requester may provide explanatory information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing public interest versus commercial interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor: Primary interest in disclosure — whether identified commercial interest is sufficiently large compared with the public interest so that disclosure is 'primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.' A waiver is justified if public-interest standard is satisfied and public interest outweighs any commercial interest. News media requesters who satisfy public interest are ordinarily presumed to have public interest as primary. Disclosure to data brokers or those compiling for economic return is not presumed to primarily serve public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial fee waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: If only some records to be released satisfy fee-waiver requirements, a waiver shall be granted for those records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for fee waiver content
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for waiver or reduction should address the fee-waiver factors listed in paragraphs (k)(2) and (3) insofar as they apply to each request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of Privacy Act subpart
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose is to establish policies/procedures for implementing the Privacy Act of 1974 to facilitate exercise of rights conferred and to ensure protection of privacy for individuals on whom USPTO maintains records; objectives include maintaining only information relevant/necessary to lawful functions and maintaining it with accuracy, relevancy, timeliness, and completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO will act promptly on inquiries/requests/appeals from U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents regardless of age; will not maintain records describing how an individual exercises First Amendment rights unless authorized by statute or pertinent to law enforcement activity; names/addresses not sold or rented unless specifically authorized by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration of Privacy Act
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart is administered by the Privacy Officer of USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters outside the scope of the Privacy Act subpart
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside scope: (1) requests for records not pertaining to the individual making the request; (2) requests involving information in a record/file but not within scope of a system of records notice; (3) requests to correct a record where a grievance procedure is available and has been or will be used (selection of grievance procedure waives use of Privacy Act procedures); (4) requests for employee-employer services and counseling routinely granted prior to the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of requests pertaining to an individual
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for records that pertains to the individual making the request (or to the individual about whom the request is made if requester is parent/guardian) shall be processed under the Privacy Act and this subpart and under FOIA and USPTO FOIA regulations, regardless of whether the Act or FOIA is mentioned in the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act definitions and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms used in the subpart that are defined in 5 U.S.C. 552a have the same meaning; additional definitions include 'Act' (Privacy Act), 'Appeal' (request to review/reverse initial denial of correction/amendment), 'USPTO', 'Inquiry', 'Person', 'Privacy Officer', 'Request for access', and 'Request for correction or amendment'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for making Privacy Act inquiries — who may submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual, regardless of age, who is a U.S. citizen or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence may submit an inquiry to USPTO (in person at specified address or by mail to the Privacy Officer or official identified in system-of-records notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If individual believes USPTO maintains a record but does not know which system, the Privacy Officer will provide assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act inquiry mailing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Inquiries submitted by mail should include the words 'PRIVACY ACT INQUIRY' in capital letters at the top of the letter and on the face of the envelope. USPTO reserves right to require identification procedures where warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to include in inquiries requesting record existence or access
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting determination whether USPTO has a record or access/copy, the inquiry should include: (1) name of individual whose record is sought; (2) citizenship or lawful residence status; (3) identifying data to help locate record (maiden name, license number, employment period/place); (4) description of record sought and record system name if known; (5) action requested (notification of rights, determination of existence, access, or copy); (6) guardianship documentation if requester is guardian/parent; (7) requester's printed name, signature, address, telephone number (optional); (8) date; (9) certification by notary or official if conditions in (b)(9)(i)-(iii) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification required only for certain types of requests (notification that record exists, access, or copy) when record is not available under FOIA and requester cannot appear for identity verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling misaddressed inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Any inquiry not addressed or marked as specified will be so addressed/marked by USPTO personnel and forwarded to the Privacy Officer; such misaddressed inquiries will not be deemed 'received' for response-time measurement until actual receipt by the Privacy Officer. The Privacy Officer shall notify the individual that the inquiry was improperly addressed and provide the date it was received at the proper address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time for Privacy Act inquiries and control numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inquiry shall be acted on promptly; every effort will be made to respond within ten working days of receipt. If a response cannot be made within ten working days, the Privacy Officer shall send an acknowledgment during that period providing status and any needed further information. First correspondence will contain USPTO control number assigned to the request, and requester should use that number in future contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Privacy Officer fails to send an acknowledgment within ten working days, the requester may ask the General Counsel to take corrective action; failure to send acknowledgment does not confer administrative finality for judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reason required for inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual shall not be required to state a reason or otherwise justify his or her inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation on systems of records notices published by other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain agencies publish notices of systems of records with Government-wide application; provisions of this section should be followed in making inquiries about such records; exemptions determined by an agency publishing a general notice shall be invoked and applied by USPTO after consultation as necessary with that agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix to this part lists agencies known to publish such notices and types of records covered.
